paragraphs.text: Bava Batra 21a: ‘What was this ordinance? As Rav Yehuda says that Rav says: Truly, that man is remembered for the good, and his name is Yehoshua ben Gamla. If not for him the Torah would have been forgotten from the Jewish people. Initially, whoever had a father would have his father teach him Torah, and whoever did not have a father would not learn Torah at all. The Gemara explains: What verse did they interpret homiletically that allowed them to conduct themselves in this manner? They interpreted the verse that states: “And you shall teach them [otam] to your sons” (Deuteronomy 11:19), to mean: And you yourselves [atem] shall teach, i.e., you fathers shall teach your sons.’ Context and connection to Divrei Chalomot: In Divrei Chalomot 2, Rav Tzadok cites this talmudic and aggadic-halakhic source (Bava Batra 21a) to illuminate his dream-vision and Torah exposition here (“and I dreamed that the plain meaning is: there are times when contention arises in the manner of (Bava Batra 21a) "the jealousy of scholars increases wisdom," and a dispute for the sake of Heaven, which is...”), showing how the translated source sheds light on nocturnal Torah insights, the elevation of the soul's faculties during sleep, and the inner secrets of the Oral Torah developed in Divrei Chalomot.
